page: Microsoft Azure L24aos_v5 is a storage-optimized virtual machine instance deployed on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It runs on x86_64 AMD processors, offering 24 dedicated vCPUs combined with 192.0 GB of RAM. This configuration provides a consistent allocation of 8.0 GB of memory per core, delivering high capacity for data-intensive processing tasks without graphic accelerator assistance, as it includes 0 GPUs.

A primary technical characteristic of the L24aos_v5 is its direct-attached NVMe SSD storage tier, bundled with 17,281 GB of local NVMe capacity. The instance also supports Premium Storage configurations, accommodating configurations that require robust I/O throughput directly connected to the host system. Complimentary public IPv4 addresses are not included with the virtual machine.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the instance targets density across local storage footprint and system memory. By integrating 17,281 GB of NVMe SSD capacity directly on host nodes alongside a generous 1:8 core-to-memory ratio, it minimizes the reliance on separate provisioned network block storage pools for data workloads requiring massive fast scratch disk or working directories. The architecture trades off specialized hardware accelerators and burst capabilities in favor of predictable, dedicated core performance.

The Microsoft Azure L24aos_v5 is structured for large-scale data systems. Key workload fits include distributed NoSQL databases, transactional data warehouses, large-footprint Elasticsearch or OpenSearch clusters, big data analytics engines, and cache systems requiring direct access to extensive local NVMe storage and large system memory arrays.
